rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The material life-law says every animal emerges from an initially shaped matter, identified as protoplasm.
rows.anchor: Her hayvan ilk tasvir edilmiş olan bir maddeden, bir madde-i musavvere-i ûlâ, ‘protoplazma’dan çıkar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This biological law is created and began only after the earth formed and animals appeared; it is not eternal.
rows.anchor: Çünkü arzın teşekkülünden ve üzerinde hayvânâtın zuhûrundan sonra başlamıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first shaped matter has been created and formed successively, and the first matter of each human formed in a womb is new.
rows.anchor: Madde-i musavvere-i ûlâ ezelî değil, o vakitten beri peyderpey halk u tasvir olunmaktadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The laws governing formation of first matter belong to chemistry and physics before biology, and mark the boundary between organic and inorganic chemistry.
rows.anchor: Bunun kānûn-ı tasvîri ilm-i hayâtın değil, ondan evvel ilm-i kimyânın ve fiziğin kanunlarındandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each new form enters existence afresh through the Creator's sustaining creative power; unformed matter itself has no actual existence apart from that power's manifestation.
rows.anchor: Madde-i gayr-i musavvere ise fiilen mevcud değildir. O da bu kudretin tecellîsine râci‘dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural laws describe the route by which an effect occurs, not the effective agent itself.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı kavânîn-i tabî‘iye tâbiri müessirin değil, tarîk-i te’sîrin ifadesidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natures differ, but nature has one source in creation and effect; nature means regularity, whose most general law is regularity itself.
rows.anchor: Tabiat, muttarid olan demektir. Ve bunun en umûmî kanunu ıttırad kanunudur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variety of natures and the processes of selection and natural development prove that God's one power governs nature and brings them about.
rows.anchor: tabâi‘muhtelif, hâlbuki mebde’-i tabiat birdir ki o da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator's formation of first matter depends on no external condition, and no power opposes His power.
rows.anchor: ilk maddenin tasvîri, hâricî hiçbir şart ile meşrut değildir ve o kudretin mukabilinde hiçbir kudret yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who forms people in wombs is the Almighty Creator, possessing the power of the Living, Self-Subsisting One.
rows.anchor: insanları erhâmda tasvir eden Hâlık-ı Musavvir böyle bir kudret-i bâliğaya mâlik bir Hayy u Kayyûm’dur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God acts as a free agent in creation and formation, not under compulsion or necessity; He acts through knowledge and will.
rows.anchor: Hâlık-ı Musavvir, bu tekvîn ü tasvîrde mecbur ve muztar değil fâ‘il-i muhtârdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving each person a distinct form reflects God's will, not prior conditions, an overriding fate, or inability to choose another form.
rows.anchor: Zeyd’e falan sureti, Amr’a fülan sureti vermesi, her şahsı bir ta‘ayyün-i mahsûsa mazhar etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The succession and replacement of forms is neither necessary nature nor uncaused; it expresses the choice and will of a free agent with knowledge and boundless power.
rows.anchor: bir fâ‘il-i muhtârın tercîhi ve iradesi eseridir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If forms were necessary, free and varied uses, differing natures, opposing natural laws, sexual variation from one seed, and life itself could not occur.
rows.anchor: bir taş, yerinden koparılıp iki muhtelif maksad için isti‘mâl edilemez, tabâyi‘ ihtilâf edemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What are called errors of nature are not defects in perfect order and power; they are evidence that nature and parents are not the true agents and that the Creator wills.
rows.anchor: bir noksan değil, tabiatın vâlid ve vâlidenin müessir-i hakīkī olmadıklarını ve Hâlık’ın iradesini gösteren şevâhid-i sanattırlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nature's failures reveal its ignorance and impotence and refute blind necessary regularity as the first principle, thereby proving a perfect free agent.
rows.anchor: tabiatın mebde’-i evvel olması nazariyesini ibtal ederek ekmel bir fâ‘il-i muhtârı isbat eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither particular nor universal nature is a complete cause; both are regularities of an originating creation made by the Creator's power and will.
rows.anchor: ne tabî‘at-i cüz’iye ne de tabî‘at-ı külliye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural regularity must be understood under a fuller law of causality and adjusted by the law of will; God can modify the nature He gives creatures.
rows.anchor: Ittırâd-ı tabîat kanunu, ekmel bir illiyet kanununun taht-ı tâbi‘iyetine verilerek irade kanunuyla ta‘dîlen mütalaa edilmedikçe hakka erilemez.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heredity names the succession of similar but nonidentical forms through changing regularity, and is a route for species survival, selection, development, and decline.
rows.anchor: bir ıttırâd-ı mütehavvil ile halef olması aynen bir ıttırad ve intikal gibi mülâhaza edilerek veraset tâbir edilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heredity concerns transformation as well as preservation, and is considered through the persistence of causes alongside change in their effects.
rows.anchor: veraset kanunu yalnız tahaffuz ve bekā kanunu değil, aynı zamanda tehavvül kanunuyla da alâkadardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No effect can exceed its cause; hereditary succession expresses the true cause's persistence and its fresh voluntary effect at every moment of transformation.
rows.anchor: illet-i hakīkiyenin bekāsını ve ıstıfâ ve tekâmül arz eden her lahza-i tehavvülde onun re’sen bir te’sîr-i irâdîsini ifade eyler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true agent's production of effects is creation, not a birth that diminishes the agent; knowing the Maker lies in affirming relations among effects, not imagining them.
rows.anchor: müessir-i hakīkīnin eserini verişi kendinden bir şey zâyi‘eden bir tevlid değil, bir hilkattir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reproduction is one manifestation of creation, and every new form in the chain of succession expresses a fresh original nature.
rows.anchor: Tevlid de halkın sûret-i tezahürlerinden birisidir. Silsile-i tevâlîde her sûret-i cedîde re’sen bir fıtrat ifade eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heredity is resemblance and succession grounded in a new act of the true cause, not a necessary transfer from one nature to another; it remains open to change.
rows.anchor: Veraset bir fıtratın diğer bir fıtrata aynen bir intikāl-i zarûrîsi değil, illet-i hakīkiyenin te’sîr-i cedîdine müstenid bir müşabeheti ve bir nevi istihlâfıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An accidental excellence or defect in a predecessor can become essential in a successor, but this is not necessary.
rows.anchor: mukaddemin kemâl veya noksan bir ‘arazîsi, tâlî de bir zâtî olabilir. Fakat olması zarûrî değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child's syphilis is not the identical disease transferred from the father, but a new occurrence of a disease of the same kind.
rows.anchor: babadaki marazın aynen bir intikali değil, çocukta onun nev‘inden bir marazın re’sen husûlüdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child's first shaped matter may contain the basis of a similar disease while being formed in the father's loins, but this is never necessary for the Creator.
rows.anchor: onun içine aynen o maraz mikrobu değil, fakat o mikrobun da bir madde-i musavvere-i ûlâsı derc edilmiş bulunabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inherited nature is a possible law: an infertile father may have a fertile child, just as a blind or syphilitic father need not have a child with the same condition; God may alter it.
rows.anchor: A‘mâ bir babanın evlâdı a‘mâ olmak lâzım gelmediği gibi firengili bir babanın evlâdı da behemehâl firengili olmak zarûrî değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question of inherited original sin belongs to heredity: Adam's nature did not intrinsically contain sin, though it could contain the capacity to sin, since sin concerns acts of will.
rows.anchor: fıtrat-ı Âdem’de zenb hiçbir zaman zâtî olarak dâhil değildir. Onda zâtî olarak nihâyet kābiliyyet-i zenb bulunabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated sin and habit may turn sin into an individual's nature, but God can create each child's nature afresh in the womb and remove parental traits, illness, or sin, making the child innocent like prophets.
rows.anchor: babasındaki husûsî tabiatı, marazı, zenbi evlâdından tamamen silerek enbiyâ gibi masum olarak yaratmaya kādir olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may later forgive, cancel the causal link between an act and punishment, nullify the act's effect or guilt, and turn what was harmful yesterday into benefit tomorrow.
rows.anchor: Fiili hükümsüz bırakır veya fiilin cürmiyetini ref‘eder de dün muzır olanı yarın nâfi‘yapar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claiming that God cannot forgive inherited sin violates divine majesty and sustaining power; even descendants of unbelievers can become believers, and God forgives unbelief through repentance and faith, while punishment is for persistence.
rows.anchor: kâfirlerden doğan kimseler bile bundan çıkıp şeref-i iman ile müşerref olabilirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is all-encompassing in knowledge, almighty in power, effective in will, Living and Sustaining, and the Mighty and Wise; none is divine but He.
rows.anchor: Allah böyle bir ilm-i muhît, bir kudret-i bâliğa, bir irâde-i nâfize ile Hayy u Kayyûm Hâlık-ı Musavvir olan bir Azîz ü Hakîm’dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus formed in Mary's womb is neither God nor God's son, but Mary's human son and God's creature, formed with a prophetic nature; miracles and knowledge of hidden matters do not remove his humanity.
rows.anchor: O, Meryem’in oğlu ve Allah’ın mahlûku bir beşerdir. Ancak fıtrat-ı nübüvvet ile tasvir olunmuş bir beşerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus's first matter need not have been made outside Mary's womb, and neither that matter nor his spirit may be conceived as emanating by begetting from the Living Sustainer.
rows.anchor: onun madde-i musavvere-i ûlâsı behemehâl rahm-i Meryem’in hâricinde yaratılması zarûrî olmadığı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Begetting requires an internal formation and diminishes the begetter, whereas the Living Sustainer cannot diminish or perish.
rows.anchor: tevlid hem müvellidin dâhilinde re’sen bir tasvîre mütevakkıftır, hem de müvellidin kıyâmını tenkīs eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One must not seize on ambiguous references such as Gospel fatherhood or Quran 4:171's spirit from Him to reject clear proofs of divine unity and fall into disbelief; scripture has a proper method of interpretation.
rows.anchor: gibi müteşâbihâtı bahane ederek küfr ü cühûda sapmamalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that after the conquest of Mecca the Prophet promised his community the sovereignties of Persia and Rome; hypocrites and Jews mocked the promise as impossible given their strength.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunuyor ki Mekke’nin fethi üzerine Resûlullah ümmetine Fars ve Rum mülklerini vaad etmiş idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Battle of the Trench, while the Prophet had assigned groups to dig, a huge rock stopped Salman al-Farisi and his companions; their iron picks broke and they asked the Prophet for help.
rows.anchor: Amr b. Avf, Selmân-ı Fârisî, Huzeyfe, Nu‘mân b. Mukrin ve ensardan altı kişi bir kırk arşında çalışıyorlardı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet struck the rock three times, each strike producing a flash; at the first he saw the palaces of Hira and Khosrow at Mada'in, and Gabriel foretold the community's conquest of them.
rows.anchor: bundan bana Hîre’nin ve Medâin-i Kisrâ’nın kasırları aydınlandı. Cibrîl de bana haber verdi ki ümmetim bunlara muhakkak galebe edecek.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second flash illuminated the red palaces of Roman territory, and Gabriel foretold that the Muslims would conquer them.
rows.anchor: arz-ı Rum’un kırmızı kasırları aydınlandı, Cibrîl de bana haber verdi ki ümmetim bunlara muhakkak galebe edecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third flash illuminated the palaces of Sana'a, and Gabriel again announced that the community would conquer them.
rows.anchor: Bundan da bana San‘â’nın kasırları aydınlandı, Cibrîl de haber verdi ki ümmetim bunlara muhakkak galebe edecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers rejoiced and expected victory after the trench was dug, while hypocrites mocked the promise as empty hope from people too frightened to fight.
rows.anchor: bu bir va‘d-i sâdıktır, ba‘de’l-hafr bize büyük bir nusret mev‘uddur!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites' charge that God's and His Messenger's promise was delusion is identified with the revelation of Quran 33:12.
rows.anchor: âyeti bunun hakkında nâzil olmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is reported that these two verses were revealed during the Trench episode or, as described above, after the conquest of Mecca; their context also points to the Christians of Najran who trusted Rome.
rows.anchor: ber vech-i bâlâ feth-i Mekke’den sonra nâzil olduğu mervîdir.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A report transmitted from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari and Ali says these verses, with the Throne Verse, the Opening, and 3:18–19, ask not to be sent to disobedient people; God promises Paradise and other rewards to anyone who recites them after every prayer, without regard to faults.
rows.anchor: Ebu Eyyûb-i Ensarî’den ve Hazret-i Ali’den rivayet olunduğu üzere Resûlullah buyurmuştur ki

rows.speaker: Saîd b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports that 360 idols around Medina fell prostrate when these verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: Saîd b. Cübeyr’den mervî olduğu üzere

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Citing a hadith qudsi in some books, Ebussuud says God holds rulers' hearts and foreheads: their obedience makes them mercy for subjects, their disobedience makes them punishment, so people should repent to God rather than curse rulers.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud tefsirinde der ki: “Bazı kitaplarda şöyle bir hadîs-i kudsî vardır:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith qudsi's meaning is the Prophetic saying that rulers are appointed over people according to what those people are like.
rows.anchor: mülûke sebb ile meşgul olmayın ve lâkin Bana tevbe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should know God in this way and offer submission and refuge to Him; the passage now addresses those who know God and seek His aid.
rows.anchor: İşte Allah’ı böyle bilmeli, böyle tanımalı ve bu tanıyışla O’na ‘arz-ı inkıyad ve ilticâ eylemelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows how diverse peoples, religions, scriptures, and consciences can unite around a foundational truth; Islam offers universal, clear, straight guidance and a law of freedom beyond Arabs and Persians.
rows.anchor: kelime-i hakta nasıl tevhid olunabilecekleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared call to worship God alone without partners or human lords is the broadest and most authoritative common conscience; religious progress lies in universality, not sectarian particularity.
rows.anchor: Terakkiyât-ı dîniye vicdanların iftirak ifade eden hususiyetlerinde değil, külliyetinde ve genişliğindedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This shared confession is the basis of freedom and equality: people must not treat one another as absolute lords, masters, or judges, but measure conduct by God's command and pleasure.
rows.anchor: İşte hürriyet ve müsâvat davasının bütün miftâh-ı halli buradadır. Birbirimizi rab, mevlâ, hâkim-i mutlak tanımayalım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There should be no pledge of obedience to anyone besides God against the right; all are God's servants and accountable to Him, and mutual allegiance is valid only from this standpoint.
rows.anchor: Allah’ı bırakıp da O’nun mâdûnunda ve hakkın hilâfında bir tâbi‘iyet mîsâkımız olmasın, hepimiz Allah’a kul olalım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must respect one another's rights and obey God-given duties for God's sake; disputes should be settled by right and law rather than anyone's personal desire.
rows.anchor: her ihtilâf mülâhaza-i hak ve kānûn-ı hak ile hallolunur. Ve hiçbir kimsenin arzû-yı mücerredi hâkim olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Therefore Jesus should be regarded as God's servant and messenger, not as Lord; popes, kings, and leaders are likewise assessed by obedience to God and pursuit of truth.
rows.anchor: Îsâ’yı da rab tanımayalım. Onu da Allah’ın bir kulu ve bir resûlü tanıyalım. Kezâlik papalar, krallar, rüesâ hep böyle

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: In response to a question, the Prophet told believing People of the Book that obeying popes and others merely because of their own words amounted to taking them as lords.
rows.anchor: Vâki‘olan bir suale karşı Resûlullah ehl-i kitabdan iman edenlere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immediate context especially addresses Christians who make Jesus Lord; translating the expression as teacher does not resolve the issue while the doctrine of Trinity remains, since God is still the true teacher in 3:48.
rows.anchor: Bugün bazı İncil tercemelerinde bunun muallim demek olduğu gösterilmiş ise de akīde-i teslis mevcud iken bu tevil kâfi olamaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book preferred division over true monotheistic unity, each claiming Abraham as their own by calling him Jewish or Christian.
rows.anchor: her biri kendilerine nisbet ederek “Yahudî idi” veya “Nasrânî idi” dediler.
